videos.title: What do you love?
videos.author: Kevin Ngo (@kevin_t_ngo)
videos.note: A cut-paper storybook drawn in code, with torn edges, crayon fill and newsprint as material. Each thing the Claude spark loves gets its own color card and lowercase caption, then they all collapse into one heart.

videos.title: The life of a fruit fly
videos.author: Kevin Ngo (@kevin_t_ngo)
videos.note: Top-down natural-history engravings alternate with dark navy embryology diagrams. Fly's-eye fisheye shots, a two-frame flight across a kitchen, and courtship drawn as looping paths.

videos.title: Claude Opus 5 drew every frame of this animation using JavaScript.
videos.author: Kevin Ngo (@kevin_t_ngo)
videos.note: Riso-print halftones on cream paper, built from one dot and its ripples. A montage of things that make sound cuts faster and faster around the same center point, until a blue dot and a pink dot orbit each other.

videos.title: The life of a honey bee
videos.author: Kevin Ngo (@kevin_t_ngo)
videos.note: A companion to the fruit fly film, recolored in honey and dark brown. Long held frames carry a time-lapse of blossoms turning into apples, and the waggle dance is decoded as a map.

videos.title: The history of the dinosaurs in under a minute
videos.author: Claude (@claudeai)
videos.note: One prompt, two models, side by side. Sonnet 5 draws flat silhouettes; Sonnet 5.5 draws in ballpoint and crayon, with captions, close-ups and a robin-to-T. rex match cut.

videos.title: Thanks @claudeai
videos.author: Kevin Ngo (@kevin_t_ngo)
videos.note: A dip pen draws a little orange creature from construction lines, then the two play: the pen joins stars into the creature's shape, draws spirographs, paints the dawn and signs 'opus 5'.

videos.title: Build 3D Websites with Kimi Code - Tutorial #4
videos.author: Kimi AI
videos.note: The first eight seconds only. A wide through a spiral-stair railing, then serif title words set into the empty wall around her, a dolly behind a red pillar for the series card, and a name label that decodes from glyph noise.

videos.title: Detection and Response | HACKING GOOGLE | Documentary EP002
videos.author: Google
videos.note: Google's documentary on how its Detection and Response team stopped North Korea's 2021 attack on security researchers. Interviews are shot in front of an LED wall that plays the film's white voxel world, so people and graphics share the frame, and the fake researcher 'Carter Edwards' is built on screen to Etta James.

videos.title: The Grand Opening: How La Cabra Opens a Café in Notion
videos.author: Notion
videos.note: La Cabra's Chelsea flagship, from raw shell to opening day. White handwritten captions are the only type, a handheld city montage keeps pace with the music, and Notion shows up only as a logo over a brownstone and a laptop on a café table.

videos.title: Consistently Excellent: How La Cabra Protects Its Craft in Every Café
videos.author: Notion
videos.note: The companion La Cabra film, about running cafés in several cities. It keeps the handwritten captions, sets Notion's location map on brand-yellow cards, and stacks AI prompt chips beside the speaker as he describes them.

videos.title: Scaling Your Craft: Monumental Labs Turns Expertise into Proposals with AI
videos.author: Notion
videos.note: A stone-carving studio drafts client proposals with a Notion agent. Phone-camera interviews in front of a marble angel, a plain screen recording of the agent writing 'Proposal – Athena Sculpture', and app icons that orbit and collapse into the Notion cube.

videos.title: Keep Projects Moving in the Background with Tasks in Gemini
videos.author: Google Gemini
videos.note: Google's Tasks film: one person after another says 'Right now, I'm…' from their own world (a dairy farm, a storm report, a sunroom full of cats) while Gemini works in the background, and the phone inserts pay off in order. It ends on 'LOOK WHAT YOU CAN DO.' set behind a jumping runner, then a Chat/Task toggle that gives way to the wordmark.

videos.title: 4 ways to tell a great story
videos.author: TED-Ed
videos.note: A TED-Ed lesson animated by Kozmonot Animation Studio entirely in flat dots on flat color. There is one hard cut in five minutes: every other change dives through a dot, a speech bubble or the O of a word, irises open or shut, or swirls in as fire. The breakdown samples 41 of its moves as flip books, with onion skins and a motion-energy timeline.

videos.title: What is sumo, and why is it so popular? - Lee Thompson
videos.author: TED-Ed
videos.note: A TED-Ed lesson on sumo's invented traditions, animated by Masayoshi Nakamura and Good General in flat ukiyo-e color under gradient skies. The motion is mostly character animation (a run cycle in place, the ring-entering ritual, throws and a long fall), joined by dives through maps, torii and tunnels of flat planes. The breakdown samples 41 moves as flip books, and the ring cycles through polygons before it settles as a circle.

videos.title: The incredible engineering of Venice - Stephanie H. Smith
videos.author: TED-Ed
videos.note: A TED-Ed lesson on how Venice was built on wooden piles in a lagoon, directed by Sofia Pashaei in flat geometric shapes with no outlines. Almost every scene change is a circle that grows from one small detail of the frame (a pile, a door, a coin) and opens on the next scene. The breakdown samples 30 moves as flip books, from piles driven by giant fingers to a flood that rises and falls against San Marco.

videos.title: Do imaginary friends make you smarter?
videos.author: TED-Ed
videos.note: A TED-Ed lesson made with the LEGO Foundation, directed by Caitlin McCarthy: Amia and her imaginary friend Zelba in flat, saturated color with thin colored outlines. Zelba is a glowing blue shape that melts and morphs into a cat, a monster, a sea serpent or a heart, and scene changes are soft-edged color blooms that grow out of a character, with memories dropping to line art. The breakdown samples 35 moves as flip books.

videos.title: How to Make an Artist Book: From Sketch to Finished Book with Perfect Binding
videos.author: The Museum of Modern Art
videos.note: MoMA's In the Studio demonstration with artist Rhea Karam, who makes a two-sided perfect-bound book of New York wall photographs from sketch to finished object. It cuts between a locked-off wide, overhead hands on a white table and shallow-focus close-ups, with eight chapter titles that rise into the top left and reference books shown as cutouts on white with small black captions. The breakdown samples 16 moves, from the scoring and binding gestures to the title reveals.

videos.title: MoMA's YouTube channel | Passionate perspectives on art
videos.author: The Museum of Modern Art
videos.note: MoMA's trailer for its YouTube channel: about 55 cuts in 68 seconds of conservators, handlers, artists and archive film, framed by on-set outtakes that open on a slate and close on 'You want me to clap?'. Half-second inserts of hands at work alternate with held beats for a joke, and the only graphics are two centered lines of white type and the wordmark, each on a cut. The breakdown samples 10 moves.

videos.title: How Two Friends Built a €1.3M Charity Platform
videos.author: Lovable
videos.note: Lovable's founder story about WeGlow. Quinten used to text his father 'I'm lighting a candle for you' before every hospital checkup, and that habit became a platform for lighting candles and donating, which the film says has raised more than €1.3 million. Two interviews in one warm room are captioned word by word in the empty wall beside each speaker, and every graphic, from a single lit candle to a glowing globe and a field of candles, turns the name into light. The breakdown covers how two text bubbles bookend the family story, how the voices are assembled, how low hits mark each reveal, and 14 moves.

videos.title: 23-Year-Old Rejected $250K To Build a Fund for South Asia
videos.author: Lovable
videos.note: A Lovable founder story about Zain, who turned down a quarter of a million in investment and went on to build Saath, a community fund for projects across South Asia. His interview, shot in a warm studio with captions that build word by word around him, alternates with a narrator over sepia photographs that bloom out of creased paper like ink. The breakdown follows how the two voices split the story, how the paper world borrows the app's own palette, and where small graphics (a cheque, two flags, color swatches) act out what he says.

videos.title: How 3 Students Built a €130K ARR AI Learning System
videos.author: Lovable
videos.note: A Lovable founder story about Isabel, Andreas and Eric, three Swedish students who say they dropped out to build Klar, an AI learning tool, and reached €130,000 ARR in its first month. Interviews in one warehouse set are cut against a scrapbook of polaroids, archive engravings and highlighted documents on black paper, and most of the speech is typeset on screen word by word. The breakdown follows how the captions become the graphics system, how a 1088 date and a university letter carry the argument, and how the music steps out for the personal lines.

videos.title: Ideas are everywhere
videos.author: Lovable
videos.note: Lovable's one-minute brand film, told by one narrator. It opens on small glowing windows of footage and rim-lit silhouettes with the reasons ideas die written across their faces, then types the Lovable name into its own prompt box and builds app after app in a single window, each change carried by a smear of the brand gradient. The breakdown follows how the voice, the on-screen words and the typed prompts share the script, and samples 14 UI moves as flip books.

videos.title: Think Together
videos.author: Notion
videos.note: Notion's two-minute manifesto against the lonely story of AI. One narrator speaks over a scrapbook of people doing things together, from the Apollo landing and the Disney studio to a campfire and a big band. The past sits as small prints on black, the lonely future arrives as headlines and empty offices, and the present fills the screen with Notion's customers. The breakdown covers how the script is split between archive audio, narration, captions and one-word cards, how image pairs and grids act out each line, and how the music steps aside for the last words.

videos.title: Meet Custom Agents: Your 24/7 AI Team
videos.author: Notion
videos.note: Notion's 71-second launch film for Custom Agents, with no voice. A conveyor of busywork piles up and blows away, then the app's own agent icons (a purple checkbox, an orange speech bubble, a teal folder) become characters that halftone hands set into the frame. Each one wipes in its own title and works real Notion screens: it routes requests to a board, answers a flood of questions and writes a status update. The night turns into a sky full of agents. The breakdown follows how three sidebar icons carry the story, and samples 12 moves.

videos.title: History of Search
videos.author: Notion
videos.note: Notion's 30-second spot for Enterprise Search, with no voice at all. Engravings of people peering through telescopes give way to the things nobody ever found (Nessie, a kraken, a UFO, Bigfoot, the Grail at the Round Table), then one unbroken stretch of product: a search for 'Project Camelot' by a user named Arthur. The breakdown follows how two lines of text, a myth montage and demo data written inside the joke carry the whole argument.

videos.title: Some Ideas Are Too Loud to Ignore
videos.author: Lovable
videos.note: Lovable's one-minute film, shot in London with the Swedish band @bokoyout (named 'Boko Yout' on screen), about an idea you cannot shake. A song follows a woman down her street, into a bookshop where the book on the counter swaps its author for the band, and past a black cab, until the band is waiting in her kitchen and she types 'Build an app for the songs in my head'. The breakdown follows how the mix opens and closes around her (muffled indoors, stripped to a tick, slammed back on a cut, thinned when the band is gone) so the song itself tells the story, and samples 8 moves as flip books.

videos.title: Jensen Huang just pulled out of Nvidia...
videos.author: Fireship
videos.note: Fireship's Code Report on the scandal it says ended Jensen Huang's run as Nvidia's CEO: five and a half minutes of one fast narrator over borrowed pictures, from news headlines and corporate filings boxed in red to labelled cutouts, memes and viewers' posts. Nearly every claim gets its source on screen, and most get a gag right after. The breakdown follows how the script is built, how found images work as both evidence and punchline, how the sponsor read grows out of the last joke, and samples 9 moves as flip books.

videos.title: Starship - Go For Orbit
videos.author: SpaceX
videos.note: SpaceX's 21-minute film of Starship Flight 14, captioned as its first orbital mission. It opens on an engine shutting down and the call not to commit to orbit, then rewinds to dawn and follows the engineers who, by the film's account, overturned that call, chose Hawaii for the landing and lit the deorbit burn. The breakdown follows how mission loop audio, interviews and subtitled room talk are cut together to build tension, and how the frames give a huge vehicle its size.
